title: MCP's New Roadmap Is a List of What's Broken
caption:
I've been blaming my own MCP server for something the protocol admits is its fault.

The new MCP roadmap landed August 22, and read straight through, it's mostly an inventory of what MCP gets wrong today: you pay tokens for every tool on a server before anyone asks a question, auth still assumes a human clicking approve in a browser, and clients are left polling for results.

I'd rather the maintainers write that down than pretend it's fine.

How many tools does your server expose?

slides.sub: MCP's new roadmap, published August 22, is largely a list of what MCP gets wrong today.

slides.title: Loaded before you ask
slides.sub: Connect a server with a hundred tools and the model pays for that whole surface before your first question.

slides.title: Auth assumes a human
slides.sub: Authorization is built around a person clicking approve in a browser. Agents running as cloud workloads have no standard identity.

slides.title: Also being rebuilt
items: Server-initiated webhooks and channels, so clients stop polling for results
Tasks (SEP-2663) matures out of extension and into the spec
One result contract, so servers know which output the client shows
